summary:
Recent developments involving the Kennedy Center closure and renewed attention to the National Guard deployment have intensified calls for D.C. statehood, with advocates arguing these incidents demonstrate the District's vulnerability to federal control. A senator has committed to prioritizing statehood, while civil rights and voting rights organizations are emphasizing the need for local self-governance in light of federal interventions over the past year.

Without statehood, D.C. residents have no voting representation in Congress, and Congress can override any law the District passes.
